mutation_summary.method: Each mutation applied by exact string replacement with a uniqueness precondition (anchor count must be 1), the target test run, then the file restored from its in-memory original and verified by SHA-256 equality. Backups were written to a real /tmp path via the bash tool, never from the sandboxed executor whose /tmp is not the host /tmp.
mutation_summary.noop_note: One anchor (C5) was first aimed at probe_admin.go where it does not occur; the harness reported it NOOP rather than silently passing, and it was re-run against run.go where fleetLeaseLookback is defined. Counted once.

harness_defect_found.finding: The first mutation run reported R1 (local-time attestation bound) as MISSED. The guard was not blind: the run had not exported TEST_MARIADB_DSN, so every mariadb subtest silently skipped and only SQLite executed, while the run still printed ok.
harness_defect_found.proof: A throwaway probe wrote the same instant as time.Now().UTC() and as a UTC+7-zoned time.Time. SQLite stored both as 2026-09-29 00:05:44+00:00 (driver normalizes). MariaDB stored 00:05:44.271906 and 07:05:44.273294 respectively (no normalization on write, despite loc=UTC in the DSN).
harness_defect_found.consequence: The .UTC() normalization in DeclareWorker and UnawareWorkers is load-bearing on MariaDB only, so a SQLite-only run of TestHubWorkerReadinessAttestationIsUtcBound proves nothing about AGENTS.md rule 6.
harness_defect_found.fix: The mutation harness now asserts the mariadb subtest reports exactly one PASS before trusting any result, and the repo mutations were re-run with the DSN exported: 9 of 9 caught.
harness_defect_found.related: Same class as the documented 'go test -run X without TEST_MARIADB_DSN silently skips' trap; recorded here because it defeated a mutation check rather than a coverage claim.

local_mode_noop_proof.claim: The gate cannot wedge a default single-pod install.
local_mode_noop_proof.reasoning: UnawareWorkers arm 1 selects monitors with worker_id IS NOT NULL and a live lease; arm 2 selects current attestations declaring an older protocol. monitors.worker_id is written only by MonitorRepo.ClaimBatch, which runs only in sharded mode (WORKER_ID set), and cleared only by ReleaseLeases. Local mode never sets it and never attests, so both arms are empty and every remote-write is allowed.
local_mode_noop_proof.verified_by: grep of every worker_id write in the mariadb and sqlite monitor repositories, plus TestShardedSchedulerWithoutReadinessStillRuns for the unattested-scheduler direction. Confirmed at process level by the passing e2e remote-assignment spec: the e2e hub runs in local mode (no WORKER_ID), so no lease roster exists and the gate allows the write.

unverified: A real mixed-version fleet: no pre-M1 worker binary was executed against this hub. The unaware-worker population is modeled by a live lease with no attestation, which is exactly what such a binary produces, but the old binary itself was not run.
Local-mode workers are not enumerable and are not covered by the gate; this is a documented detection boundary, not a tested behavior.
The residual window where an unaware worker joins AFTER a remote assignment was committed. The gate is point-in-time at write and does not re-check.
Multi-replica sharded behavior under a real rolling Kubernetes upgrade (lease handoff, replica count changes, SHARD_LEASE_TTL divergence between API and worker pods).
Load, populated partitioned migration timing/lock/disk behavior, backlog drain rate, kill points at every durable boundary, and the canary. All remain open M6 scope.
Restore-path exemption is asserted by construction and by the absence of a gate call on that path; no end-to-end backup-import-while-fleet-degraded process test was run in this slice.

The CLI assign gate is verified by decision-logic unit tests plus a source-ordering assertion on the call site; `RunProbeAdmin assign` was not driven end to end, which would need a provisioned key file, an initialized installation and an enrolled probe.

cli_path_finding.finding: Auditing callers of ProbeAssignmentWriter.ReplaceWithBindings found internal/bootstrap/probe_admin.go's `assign` command writing the desired set directly through repository.NewProbeAssignmentStore, bypassing the service-level gate. It is a genuine remote-activation path and the tool an operator reaches for mid-rollout.
cli_path_finding.found_by: grep of every ReplaceWithBindings / CreateMonitorWithAssignments / Restore caller in non-test source, to verify the documented Restore exemption rather than to look for this.
cli_path_finding.fix: probeAdminAssignGate wraps services.FleetActivationGate with fleetLeaseLookback(cfg) and runs before the write; refusals name the straggler workers, which is appropriate for an operator console and deliberately not done in the HTTP response body.
cli_path_finding.call_site_guard: TestProbeAdminAssignConsultsTheFleetGate asserts the invocation exists, is wired to repos.hubWorkerReadiness, and precedes ReplaceWithBindings in the assign block. A decision-logic unit test alone cannot catch deletion of the call.
cli_path_finding.restore_still_exempt: Restore is reached only from backup_service.go and configascode.go directly on the repository port, never through a gated service method, so the documented exemption holds by construction.
